Definition: from a presumed compound of G2095 and the base of G1380; satisfaction, i.e. (subjectively) delight, or (objectively) kindness, wish, purpose:--desire, good pleasure (will), X seem good.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, eudokía is the word for desire, good pleasure (will), X seem good. In Matthew 11:26, the text says "for so it seemed good in thy sight." In Luke 2:14, the text says "good will toward men."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, eudokía is a reminder that grace is God giving what we could never earn, and never taking it back. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Birth of Jesus; The Shepherds Visit the Newborn Jesus
